title: Hardware Trust Anchors on a Modern System
description: An interactive SVG board diagram of four hardware trust anchors — TEE region, Secure Enclave coprocessor, discrete TPM, and external HSM — with a Hardware Root of Trust badge and hover tooltips giving each anchor's capability and threat model.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity

learningObjectives: Identify the four hardware trust anchors on a modern system and where each lives.
Explain why a root of trust must be anchored in silicon, not software.
Compare the threat model and assurance level of TEE, Secure Enclave, TPM, and HSM.

instructionalStrategies: Hover each anchor and have students place it on a spectrum from on-die to off-board.
Ask students which anchor still protects a key when the OS is fully compromised, and why.

assessmentQuestions.question: Why is the TEE region drawn with an amber outline instead of solid blue?
A laptop's OS is compromised by malware. Which trust anchors can still protect a sealed key, and which cannot?
